# Winter round checklist

Typed this up after the December 2025 round because I kept forgetting steps
between sites and it is easier to have a list on the phone than to ask
someone else every time. Not official rules — just what I actually do when
the tracks are muddy and the light goes at four.

## Before leaving home

Pack two spare batteries even if the plan is only to read voltages. Last
winter I needed a third at AWS-07 and had to come back the following week.
Gloves, head torch, and a towel for wiping enclosure lids. Check the
inventory page for firmware mismatches so you are not surprised on site.

Message the check-in contact with the station list and ETA. If the round
includes AWS-10 or AWS-12, say so explicitly because both are awkward in
low light.

## At each enclosure

Wipe condensation off the inside of the lid before opening fully; water
drips on the board otherwise. Read the battery voltage from the Kestrel
status screen and write it in the pocket notebook — do not trust memory for
twelve numbers. Anything under 12.1 V on a cold day goes on the swap list
for next visit unless it has dropped more than 0.3 V since the last reading.

Check that the solar panel cable gland has not worked loose. Tighten by
hand only. Look at the rain gauge funnel for leaf blockage; a stuffed funnel
looks like drought in the readings and wastes everyone's time later.

## Stations I double-check

AWS-07 gets an extra look because of the January outage. AWS-08 sits in a
fold that holds water around the base — lift the enclosure slightly on the
packing foam if the bottom feels soggy. AWS-09 and AWS-10 are the radio
weak spots; if the packet counter on the logger has not moved since the
last visit, note it before climbing down.

## After the round

Photograph the notebook page and drop it in the shared album. Update battery
replacement dates if anything was swapped. Send the return check-in message
before stopping for tea on the way home, not after, because once you sit
down the message gets forgotten until someone asks.
